transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m not sure if this is the right sort of thing to come in for, but I just can’t seem to get things in order anymore. My kitchen table is just covered—my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, little lists I started and didn’t finish. I sit down to try to sort it out, and I honestly don’t know which thing to do first. Then somehow the whole day is gone, and I haven’t really done any of it.
Do you find yourself forgetting things that you would normally remember?

Yes… I do, more than I’d like to admit. It’s probably little things, but they add up. I’ve missed returning phone calls, and I’ve left bills sitting under a stack of mail until I found them later. I’ve also forgotten errands I told my daughter I’d do, which makes me feel awful. And more than once I realized too late that I never confirmed one of my husband’s appointments. I know that sounds careless… I’m trying, I really am.
Do you have trouble focusing on tasks or paying attention to what you're doing?

Yes… I think I do. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but if the television is on in the next room, or if a couple of people start talking near me at the senior center, my mind just sort of goes over there. Then I look back down at what I was writing or trying to plan, and I’ve lost my place. It’s embarrassing, really. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you have trouble keeping your living or work space organized?

Yes… yes, I do. I try not to let it get too bad, but lately my kitchen table especially has just become this sort of landing place for everything—my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, little lists I start and then don’t finish.

I’ll sit down meaning to sort it all out, and then I just… I don’t know which pile to start with or what matters most. And before I know it, the day has gone by and it’s still sitting there. I know it probably sounds like ordinary clutter, but it feels like I can’t get it in order.
Do you find yourself repeating questions or conversations because you've forgotten that you already had them?

I’m not sure… I don’t think that’s been a big problem, at least not that anyone has pointed out to me. I might ask for clarification sometimes, but repeating whole conversations because I’ve forgotten them? I don’t think so. If that were happening, my daughter would probably tell me… I hope. Is that okay to say?
Do you ever feel mentally foggy or confused, like your thinking is cloudy or unclear?

I’m not sure I’d call it confused, exactly. I don’t usually feel like I don’t know what’s going on. Maybe some days I feel a little slower getting my thoughts together, but “foggy” sounds… well, stronger than what I’d want to say. I haven’t really noticed it as a main problem. Does that make sense?
Do you ever struggle to find the right words when you're trying to express yourself?

Hmm… finding the right words? Not usually, I don’t think. I mean, everyone has that thing where a word is on the tip of your tongue now and then, especially at my age, but I wouldn’t say it happens enough that I’m worried about it.

I may pause sometimes to think how to say something, but I don’t feel like I’m losing words or anything like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you have trouble planning out tasks or projects from start to finish?

Yes… I think that’s actually a big part of why I came in, though I feel a little embarrassed saying it.

I used to be able to keep things in some kind of order, but lately I just… I’ll sit at the kitchen table and there are papers everywhere — my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, senior-center notes, little lists I started and didn’t finish — and I honestly don’t know which thing to do first. I’ll mean to sort it out, but then the whole day can go by and I’ve barely made a dent.

I don’t know if that counts as planning exactly, but it feels like I can’t get things in order from beginning to end anymore. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do you have trouble remembering recent events or learning new information?

I… I wouldn’t say I can’t learn anything new, exactly. But yes, with recent things I do have trouble, more than I like to admit.

I’ve missed returning calls, and I’ll leave a bill sitting under a stack of mail and then find it later and feel awful. I’ve forgotten errands I told my daughter I would do, which is embarrassing. And more than once I’ve realized too late that I never confirmed one of my husband’s appointments.

I try to write things down, but somehow things still slip. Is that the kind of remembering you mean?
Do you often struggle to find the right words when speaking or writing?

I don’t think so… not often, anyway. I mean, I might pause now and then or lose my train for a second, but I haven’t really noticed struggling to find words when I’m talking or writing.

Unless you mean something more subtle? I don’t want to answer wrong, but it’s not something that feels like a main problem for me.
Have your symptoms caused any problems for you at home, at work, or in your relationships with others?

Yes… I suppose it has, though I don’t like to make it sound worse than it is.

At home, my daughter has started sort of… double-checking me. Bills, appointments, things like that. She’s kind about it, but I can tell she doesn’t really trust that I’ll keep it all straight by myself anymore. That’s hard to admit.

And I did give up leading a big event at the senior center. I told people it was just getting to be too much, which is true, but really I was afraid I’d miss something important or let everyone down.

So… yes, it has caused problems. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you find yourself often having trouble thinking of the right word when speaking?

No, I don’t think that’s really one of my problems. I might pause if I’m tired or distracted, but I’m not usually searching for words or unable to say what I mean.

At least, I haven’t noticed it as something frequent. Is that okay—does that answer it?
Do you have difficulty breaking down large tasks into smaller, manageable steps?

Yes… I think that’s actually a big part of why I came in, though I feel a little embarrassed saying it.

I used to be able to sort things out, but now I’ll sit at my kitchen table with my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, senior-center notes, and these half-finished lists, and I just… don’t know where to start. I’ll think, “Well, I should do this first,” and then another paper catches my eye, and before I know it the whole day has gone by and nothing is really done.

It’s not that the tasks are impossible, exactly. It’s more that I can’t seem to get them into order or break them down the way I should. Does that make sense?
Do you have trouble keeping track of your belongings or often misplace things?

Yes… I do, more than I’d like to admit.

I’m forever hunting for things I just had in my hand—my car keys, my reading glasses, appointment cards, that sort of thing. Sometimes it’s a recipe I need for the church supper, or the folder I’m supposed to take to the doctor’s office, and I’ll be sure I put it somewhere sensible… but then I can’t find it.

I know everyone misplaces things, so I don’t want to make too much of it, but it does happen to me quite a lot. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your daily life or relationships that you think might be related to the problems you're experiencing with organization and memory?

Yes… there have been a couple of changes, I suppose. I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, but I did step back from leading a big event at the senior center. I just couldn’t keep all the pieces straight the way I needed to, and I was afraid I’d let people down.

And my daughter has started… well, she double-checks the bills and appointments now. She’s kind about it, but I think she doesn’t fully trust me to manage it all on my own anymore. That’s hard to say out loud.

Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you often struggle to find the right words when writing, like in notes or letters?

Hmm… I don’t think so, not especially. I mean, I might pause over a note or a card and wonder how to phrase something politely, but I’ve always been a little that way.

I haven’t really noticed that I can’t find the words, exactly. It’s more… well, I’m not sure. But no, I don’t think word-finding when I’m writing is one of the bigger problems. Is that helpful?
Do you often find yourself struggling to find the right words when you're speaking spontaneously, like in the middle of a conversation?

I don’t think so… not in any way that stands out to me. I mean, sometimes I’ll pause and think, “Oh, what was the name of that place?” or something like that, but I think that happens to most people, doesn’t it?

In conversation, I’m usually able to say what I mean. At least, I haven’t noticed people having trouble understanding me or anything like that. So I’d say no, not often. Is that all right?
Have you felt like your difficulties with organization, memory, and focus have significantly impacted your overall well-being or daily life?

Yes… I think it has, though I wish it hadn’t. I try not to make too much of it, but it’s changed things.

I had to give up leading that big event at the senior center because I just couldn’t keep all the details straight, and that was really upsetting. And my daughter has started checking behind me with bills and appointments—not in an unkind way, but because she doesn’t really trust that I’ll remember everything on my own now.

So yes, I suppose it has affected my daily life quite a bit. Is that what you mean?
Have you experienced any significant stress, anxiety, or emotional difficulties recently?

I’m not sure I’d call it significant, exactly. I mean, everyone has stress, don’t they? I do get a bit upset or worried sometimes when I feel like I’m not keeping up the way I used to, but I try not to dwell on it.

I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. It’s just… a little discouraging at times, I suppose. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you think your difficulties with memory, organization, and focus have gotten noticeably worse over the past few months or years?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to exaggerate it, but it’s been noticeably more troublesome for about a year or so—maybe a year and three months.

It seemed to become harder when my husband started needing regular help with his appointments and daily arrangements. I suppose having more to keep track of made it more obvious. Does that make sense?
